reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates that a 10–20 μm Ni coating deposited by magnetron sputtering on diamond particles forms a solid solution interlayer with an HEA matrix, improving interfacial bonding and reducing defects. However, the evidence is for a diamond/HEA system, not W–Cu, and reports mechanical properties, not thermal conductivity. The key premises about thermal conductivity improvement and transferability to W–Cu are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Magnetron sputtering can deposit a uniform 10–20 μm Ni coating on particles
A Ni coating on a reinforcing phase can form a solid solution interlayer with a matrix upon sintering/annealing
Such a Ni-based interlayer improves interfacial bonding and reduces interfacial defects (voids, cracks)
Improved interfacial bonding and reduced defects enhance composite thermal conductivity
The coating and annealing approach is transferable from diamond/HEA to W–Cu systems
